claims.text: Single-phase fcc FeCoNi and related high-entropy-alloy derivatives typically have coercive fields below approximately 100 Oe.
Substituting approximately 10 at% Pt into FeCoNi will promote local L10 ordering.
Rapid solidification followed by controlled annealing will favor nanoscale precipitation of the new ordered phase.
Approximately 10 at% Pt substitution will produce nanoscale L10-ordered precipitates embedded in an fcc matrix.
The L10 phase has higher magnetocrystalline anisotropy than the fcc phase.
The L10 precipitates will behave as hard magnetic nanodomains within the soft fcc matrix.
The hard L10 nanodomains will be exchange coupled to the remaining soft fcc matrix.
Exchange coupling between the L10 nanodomains and fcc matrix will increase domain-wall pinning.
Increased domain-wall pinning will raise the alloy's coercive field.
The Pt-modified alloy may have a coercive field above 300 Oe rather than below 100 Oe.
The Pt-modified alloy will retain high saturation magnetization with only minimal compromise relative to the baseline.
The proposed effect is applicable to both bulk alloys and thin films made under controlled rapid-solidification and annealing conditions.
The magnitude of coercivity enhancement depends on processing parameters and phase distribution.
The optimal Pt concentration is dependent on processing and remains undetermined.

contradictions.description: A coercive field above 300 Oe is presented only as a tentative example ('potentially' and 'e.g.'), while failure to exceed approximately 300 Oe is treated as a decisive falsification threshold despite acknowledged uncertainty in the enhancement magnitude.
